sentences.text: The present claim petition is filed by the petitioner, through her representative, claiming compensation of .50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 15.03.2022 at about 07.30 a.m., when she was walking on footpath by the side of Chintamani-Kolar Road, Kolar Cross, Chintamani Town, Chikkaballapura District, a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EA- 6357, ridden by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to her.

Due to the accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, she was shifted to Govt. Hospital, Chintamani and then referred to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent .2,00,000/-
towards medical and conveyances expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Tailor and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 has also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further contended that the rider of motor cycle was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.

Further the alleged accident occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner alone, who was walking on the road and trying to cross the road unmindfully and without having proper look out for vehicular movements and suddenly came to the road by running, where there is no provision for pedestrian crossing near the place of accident and she came to contact some unknown vehicle and sustained injuries.
Further contended that the accident did not take place due to rashness or negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
The offending vehicle is not involved in the cause of accident.

Further respondent No.2 admitted the aspect of issue of policy of insurance in favour of first respondent in respect of motor cycle and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:

6. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the Medical Record Officer at Nimhans Hospital got examined as PW.1, Dr.Jamuna Rajeshwaran got examined as PW.2, representative/son of petitioner got examined as PW.3 and Dr.N.R.Jayanthi at Chintamani Govt. On the other hand, PSI Chintamani got examined as RW.1 and the respondent insurance company examined its Assistant Manager as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to 6 and closed their side of evidence.

7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;

Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 15.03.2022 at about 07.30 a.m., accident occurred at Kolar Cross, Chintamani Town, Chikkaballapura District, while she was walking on footpath, due to the rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 by its rider in which she sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 by its rider, the son of petitioner has examined himself as PW.3.
In the chief examination, PW.3 deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.3 nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.3 to disprove the case of petitioner.
11. Further, in order to prove the accident, PW.3 has produced Ex.P.4 and P.5, FIR and first information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.5 first information statement, son of petitioner has Mangamma vs Chandrappa on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51343032/
3 lodged complaint with police on 11.04.2022 pertaining to the accident occurred on 15.03.2022.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.4 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The FIR has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle which does not appear to have been questioned or challenged.
12. The petitioner also furnished spot panchanama, which is marked as Ex.P.6.
The said document discloses the aspect of police visiting the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials to show that the facts at the place of accident, as described in the mahazar, are contrary to the actual facts.
Ex.P.8 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to vehicle are mentioned.
The vehicle will be inspected after seizure of the same by the police.
The said document indicates the aspect of seizure of vehicle by the police on the ground of its involvement in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the seizure procedure conducted by the police.
The said document indicates the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
13. Ex.P.9 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.10.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.3 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioner could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
14. Further, on perusal of the materials, there appears to be delay of 28 days in lodging first information statement.
The accident occurred on 15.03.2022.
As per Ex.P.4, first information statement, son of petitioner has lodged complaint with police on 11.04.2022.
As per the materials placed on record, there was 28 days delay in lodging complaint.
The complainant in his complaint explained that he was at the hospital along with his mother while she was taking treatment as an inpatient and thereafter lodged the complaint with the police.
Further, on perusal of hospital documents placed by the petitioner, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to the hospital.

The materials on record disclose that the petitioner sustained serious injuries due to the Mangamma vs Chandrappa on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51343032/
4 accident.

sentences.text: Due to the severe injuries, the present petition is filed through the representative.
In general parlance, the injured as well as his family members think about providing best treatment to the patient rather than to lodge complaint before the police.
As the petitioner appears to have sustained serious injuries due to the accident, she or her family member cannot be expected to lodge complaint to the police rather than availing treatment.
Availing of treatment will be the priority for the injured rather than to file complaint.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana in (2011) 4 SCC 693, held that delay in lodging a FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimants case.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this tribunal cannot dismiss the petition only on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.
No materials are placed to create doubt about contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of respondent in the cause of accident.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
15. It is the specific contention of respondent No.2 that the offending vehicle has not been involved in the accident and it has been falsely implicated.
In order to substantiate the said contention, the respondent No.2 got examined the I.O as RW.1.
RW.1 stated the aspect of conducting the investigation and filing the final report against the rider of the offending vehicle.
RW.1 clearly stated in his evidence that after the investigation, the negligence is found on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle and as such, the final report is filing against him.

RW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent No.2 and in the cross examination, nothing to substantiate the contention of respondent No.2 related to false implication of offending vehicle could be elicited.

Further, RW.1 clearly stated that he seized the offending vehicle and filed final report against the said vehicle as the materials collected during the investigation pointed towards the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
The evidence of RW.1 will not be of much assistance to the respondents in disproving the contention of the petitioner and to substantiate the aspect of implication of vehicle.
16. Further, the petitioner furnished the IMV Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8.
The said document discloses the aspect of damages caused to the offending vehicle.
If the vehicle is not involved in the accident, then the damages as mentioned in the IMV Report could not have been caused.

Further,
the driver or owner of the offending vehicle could have explained the manner in which the damages,
as mentioned in Ex.P.8, were caused to the vehicle.
The materials on record do not disclose any explanation being provided about the manner in which the damages were caused to the offending vehicle, if it is not involved in the accident.
Ex.P.8 clearly indicates the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of any relationship between the petitioner and owner or rider of the offending vehicle in order to consider the aspect of implication of vehicle.
The materials placed by the petitioner coupled with the evidence of RW.1 disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of the offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record disclose the involvement of the offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
17. It is pertinent to note that, the owner of the vehicle not appeared before the tribunal in spite of service of notice.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the vehicle, is considered to be a proper person to state about the involvement of the vehicle belonging to him in the accident.

But, the Mangamma vs Chandrappa on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51343032/

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 could have appeared before the tribunal and denied the contentions of petitioner regarding involvement of his vehicle and negligence of rider of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.1 not appeared before the tribunal in order to resist the claim made by the petitioner.
The contention raised by respondent No.2 regarding implication of vehicle has not been substantiated by cogent and substantive materials.
The evidence of RW.1 assists the contention of petitioner rather than the respondent No.2.
Under such circumstances, the contention of respondent No.2 that the vehicle has been falsely implicated does not appear to be sustainable.
18. In Ex.P.5, first information statement, the vehicle number is mentioned as KA-40-E-6357.
It is pertinent to note that the respondent No.2 not furnished any materials to show the existence of vehicle number as mentioned in Ex.P.2.
The registration number of vehicle is could be considered as wrongly mentioned in Ex.P.5.
Ex.P.5 is a preliminary document based on which the criminal law will be set into motion and cannot be considered as a conclusive document to consider the non- involvement of the offending vehicle.
Further the investigation conducted by I.O. indicates the aspect of involvement of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EA- 6357 and not the vehicle bearing No.KA-40-E-6357.
As stated above, no materials are placed to show the existence of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 and to show that the said vehicle has been involved in the accident.
The said aspect cannot be considered sufficient to hold that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated.
The police records and the evidence of RW.1 clearly indicate involvement of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EA-6357 and not the vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357.
As such, the contentions raised by respondents cannot be considered to have been proved with cogent and substantive materials.
19. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.4 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.

sentences.text: In order to prove the injuries sustained the petitioner has produced Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.9, wherein it discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.
The petitioner produced Ex.P.14 & 15 Discharge Summaries issued by Suma Nursing Home and NIMHANS Hospital which discloses the aspect of treatment availed by petitioner.
The petitioner examined Dr.Jamuna Rajeswaran and Dr.N.R.Jayanthi as PW.2 & 4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.3, 17 & 18.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of her current cognitive functioning for disability certification to the extent of 100%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .60,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses: The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that she took treatment at the Hospital.
The petitioner has produced 13 medical bills amounting to .52,881/- marked at Ex.P.16 and advance receipts marked at Ex.P.11 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.12.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .52,881/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 15.03.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of materials on record, it discloses that the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital as she has sustained injuries.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.14 & 15 Discharge Summaries which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 16.03.2022 to 07.04.2022 and again from 26.04.2022 & 27.04.2022 i.e., for a period of 25 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 25 days to a sum of .12,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is the resident of Vinayakanagar, Chintamani Town, Chikkaballapura District and she has admitted to hospital for treatment.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner has produced Discharge Summaries marked at Ex.P.14 & 15.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses towards conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that she was working as a Tailor and earning a sum of .20,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner has not produced any document.
The petitioner not furnished any materials to show that she was earning .20,000/- per month.

In the absence of satisfactory materials related to income of petitioner, notional income is to be considered.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .15,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended her work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .50,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, she was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also got examined Dr.Jamuna Rajeswaran, working as Professor of Neuropsychology, Nimhans Hospital, Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess the disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained brain injury and also diagnosis of post traumatic hydrocephalus was made and referred to Nimhans Hospital for neuropsychological assessment.

Further PW.2 deposed that petitioner came walking assisted by her son to testing room and she had difficulty in walking and was alert and conscious and oriented to time, place and person, rapport could be established her attention could not be aroused but difficult to sustain and was not co- operative and motivated and she could understand and follow even simple instructions but difficult instructions she could not understand,
her speech was clear and her mood was unstable and get irritable easily and her psychomotor activity was decreased and her reaction time was increased.
Further PW.2 deposed that due to head injury, battery could not be administered, vineland social maturity scale (VSMS) was administered.
On VSMS she gets an IQ of 24 indicating profound deficits in socio adaptive functions and she gets a cognitive disability of 100% according to RPWD Act, Government of India.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.3 i.e., Neuropsychological Assessment protocol.

The petitioner also examined Dr.N.R.Jayanathi, working as a Senior Specialist &
Casualty Medical Officer at Chintamani Govt Hospital, Chikkaballapura District and examined as PW.4.
PW.4/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

PW.4/Doctor has also produced documents at Ex.P.17 & 18 i.e.,
police intimation and MLC Extract.

The petitioner also examined Medical Record Officer of Nimhans Hospital,
Bengaluru as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 & 2 i.e., authorization letter and case sheet.

On consideration of evidence of PW.2 and the materials on record, the petitioner appears to be unable to do her normal activities as before.
PW.2 stated that it is difficult for the petitioner to lead a normal life.
The petitioner is stated to be suffering with problems of loss of memory, difficulty to understand difficult instructions.
In the cross examination, PW.2 stated that the condition of petitioner may improve or may worsen.
The evidence of PW.2 indicates that there is less improvement in the condition of petition and the possibilities of improvement also appears to be difficult.
The materials on record disclose that the petitioner is not able to perform her routine works.
The materials on record reveal that the petitioner requires assistance for doing her routine work.

On considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner is not able to perform her activities as before and there appear to be difficulties which cause hindrance in performing normal routine activities.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 80%.

the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 57 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '09'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 has also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Further contended that the rider of motor cycle was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
1. Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 15.03.2022 at about 07.30 a.m., Kolar Cross, Chintamani Town,
Chikkaballapura District, while she was walking on footpath, due to the rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award?
Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-

9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 15.03.2022 at about 07.30 a.m., accident occurred at Kolar Cross, Chintamani Town, Chikkaballapura District, while she was walking on footpath, due to the rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 by its rider in which she sustained grievous injuries.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Due to the severe injuries, the present petition is filed through the representative.
In general parlance, the injured as well as his family members think about providing best treatment to the patient rather than to lodge complaint before the police.
As the petitioner appears to have sustained serious injuries due to the accident, she or her family member cannot be expected to lodge complaint to the police rather than availing treatment.
Availing of treatment will be the priority for the injured rather than to file complaint.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana in (2011) 4 SCC 693, held that delay in lodging a FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimants case.
No materials are placed to create doubt about contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of respondent in the cause of accident.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
The materials on record do not disclose any explanation being provided about the manner in which the damages were caused to the offending vehicle, if it is not involved in the accident.
Ex.P.8 clearly indicates the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record do not disclose the aspect of any relationship between the petitioner and owner or rider of the offending vehicle in order to consider the aspect of implication of vehicle.
The materials placed by the petitioner coupled with the evidence of RW.1 disclose the aspect of negligence on the part of the offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The materials on record disclose the involvement of the offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondent No.1, being the owner of the vehicle, is considered to be a proper person to state about the involvement of the vehicle belonging to him in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is a preliminary document based on which the criminal law will be set into motion and cannot be considered as a conclusive document to consider the non- involvement of the offending vehicle.
Further the investigation conducted by I.O. indicates the aspect of involvement of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EA- 6357 and not the vehicle bearing No.KA-40-E-6357.
As stated above, no materials are placed to show the existence of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357 and to show that the said vehicle has been involved in the accident.
The said aspect cannot be considered sufficient to hold that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated.
The police records and the evidence of RW.1 clearly indicate involvement of vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-EA-6357 and not the vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-40-E-6357.
As such, the contentions raised by respondents cannot be considered to have been proved with cogent and substantive materials.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
The materials on record reveal that the petitioner requires assistance for doing her routine work.
On considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner is not able to perform her activities as before and there appear to be difficulties which cause hindrance in performing normal routine activities.
As per the document furnished before the Tribunal, the age of petitioner appears to be 57 years at the time of accident.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary,
the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 57 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .30,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.
